critic_notes.rationale: Economically coherent and sign-consistent (both rank legs push the composite up where returns are hypothesized low), though it is close to the known capex-investment and leverage/distress anomalies and, because the ranks are multiplied without demeaning, it will largely load on the two main effects rather than a true conditional interaction, and the double-differenced GROWTH(capx/ppent) leg is noisy for small-PP&E firms.

Construction flaw — Compustat `intan` already includes `gdwl`, so ADD(intan, gdwl) double-counts goodwill and the leg is missing/zero for a large share of firms (coverage risk), while the distress leg is a standard Ohlson/Altman-style composite, leaving little that is genuinely new.

Internally inconsistent sign logic: the conditioning leg SUMRANK(leverage, -OCF) is itself a high-distress indicator with a documented *negative* return main effect, so the undemeaned product will be dominated by distress and its natural direction contradicts the stated positive EXPECTED_SIGN.

Clean, well-specified, and sign-consistent, and the liquidity-conditioned twist on the known inventory-growth anomaly is at least modestly novel, but unscaled inventory growth times an inverse current ratio is a fairly mechanical two-anomaly product whose incremental content over inventory growth alone is unproven.

This is effectively a repackaging of three of the most heavily published anomalies (net share issuance, asset growth, low profitability) and specifically of the CMA×RMW combination, so it is both a rediscovery and largely mechanically absorbed by the FF5 benchmark used to compute ls_alpha.

Near-duplicate of "Levered Capex Surge" within the same batch (PP&E growth × a leverage proxy), with a less stable conditioning variable since `che` in the denominator explodes for cash-poor firms, and the INTERACTION_TYPE is mislabeled as "ratio" when the expression is a rank product.

This is essentially a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archive's "Liquidity-Stressed Acquisition Spend" — NEG(wcap/at) is close to a monotone restatement of lct/act, the oancf leg is identical, and swapping the acquisition level for its one-year delta on a lumpy, mostly-zero variable is a minor tweak rather than a new mechanism.

The conditioning leg is recycled verbatim from two archive signals, but the capacity-versus-demand investment leg (PP&E growing faster than sales, i.e. deteriorating capital turnover) is a genuinely different economic construct; the main risk is that ratio growth is driven by falling sales, which partially double-counts the distress conditioner.

Internally consistent and distinct from the archive's capex-acceleration variants by conditioning on the *source* of funding (cash drawdown) rather than leverage, though the capex/at leg is the plain Titman-Wei-Xie capital-investment anomaly and Δche overlaps mechanically with wcap, so incremental content may be thin.

Inventory build and declining operating cash flow are mechanically the same event (inventory is a working-capital drag on OANCF), so the product is largely a rediscovery of the Sloan accrual anomaly with a self-correlated interaction rather than an independent conditional test.

The expression matches the hypothesis and the positive sign is coherent (low investment plus improving flows), which is a legitimate structural fix to the earlier failed positive-sign idea, but Δoancf and Δwcap are highly overlapping and the construct risks collapsing into a generic free-cash-flow/low-asset-growth composite.

Labor intensity growth is a meaningfully different investment leg than raw headcount growth and addresses the prior signal's sign inconsistency, but NEG(ib/at) is a strong standalone profitability main effect that could dominate the interaction, and sales appearing in both legs invites confounding with simple sales decline.

The funding-gap level (capx − oancf, i.e. negative free cash flow to assets) is a substantively different construction from the archive's capex-growth/acceleration variants and the industry ranking is a sensible control, though the base leg is close to the known low-free-cash-flow / cash-based-profitability anomaly, so incremental content over that is the main open question.

Using the goodwill stock rather than acquisition flow is a genuinely different mechanism from the archive's aqc-based signals and the leverage-plus-loss overlay is coherent, but RANK(COALESCE(gdwl,0)) piles a large no-goodwill mass at the bottom rank, which will mechanically flatten the interaction and should be checked in coverage/portfolio-composition diagnostics.

This is essentially a recombination of components already tested in the archive (capex level from Cash-Burning Capex Commitment, −oancf/at from Cash-Flow-Strained Capex Acceleration, Δdebt/at from Debt-Financed Loss Acquisition), so it is a cosmetic variant that also overlays two well-known anomalies (asset growth/investment and net debt issuance) without a new economic distinction.

Shifting from inventory growth (Thomas–Zhang territory, already tested here) to inventory share of current assets is a legitimately different construct, but note that invt/act and che/at are mechanically complementary components of current assets, so part of the product just squares the same liquidity-composition variable and the marginal role of the −che leg should be tested separately.

Deliberately testing the underinvestment side (low capex plus old net-to-gross PPE) against the standard investment anomaly is an economically interesting, non-obvious hypothesis with a correctly signed expression, though the main risk is that the product collapses into a generic financial-distress proxy, so a distress-controlled version should be part of the follow-up.

Since wcap = act − lct, the −wcap/at leg carries essentially the same information as the lct/act leg in the already-tested Distress Hiring Mismatch (fmb_tstat = +1.12, wrong sign), making this a cosmetic proxy swap on a construction that has already failed cross-sectionally.

The two conditioning terms (NEG(pi/at) and NEG(txt/at)) are mechanically near-redundant — tax expense is largely a function of pretax income — so the "tax-loss state" collapses into a low-profitability double-count, making this a cosmetic reweighting of the archive's already-tested Cash-Flow-Strained Capex Acceleration rather than a distinct mechanism.

This is a within-family reshuffle of the archive's Liquidity-Stressed Acquisition Spend — dlc/act is a subcomponent of the already-used lct/act, and negative sales growth was already tested as a distress leg in Distress Hiring Mismatch — so it is unlikely to deliver economically distinct information.

The main effect (change in non-goodwill intangible intensity) is a genuinely new investment channel relative to the archive's goodwill-level signal and the hypothesis matches the expression's sign, though COALESCE(intan,0)/COALESCE(gdwl,0) conflates true zeros with missing data and will create a large mass point that should be diagnosed alongside coverage.

Multiplying the inventory rank by a 0/1 current-deficit indicator zeroes out most of the cross-section, producing massive ties and a degenerate long leg — an unstable portfolio construction rather than a real refinement of the already-tested Inventory Liquidity Trap.

This is close to a rediscovery of the archive's failed Resilient Capex Retrenchment (low capex × improving fundamentals), and the archive's Deferred Maintenance Distress already showed low capex earning positive alpha even in the distress state, suggesting the resilience interaction adds nothing beyond a low-capex main effect; the hypothesis also mislabels DELTA(ib/at) as "operating" profitability.

Scaling equity issuance by real investment outlay is a genuinely distinct financing-versus-investment construct not yet in the archive and is internally consistent with the negative sign, but the ratio has a near-zero/zero denominator problem that 1% winsorization will not fully tame, and it partially overlaps the known external-financing/net-issuance anomaly.

SUB(GROWTH(ppent),GROWTH(sale)) is a first-order algebraic equivalent of GROWTH(ppent/sale) already tested as "Demand-Mismatched Capacity Build" with an identical conditioning leg, so this is a cosmetic re-specification rather than a substantively different mechanism.

Because aqc is zero or missing for the large majority of firm-years, COALESCE(aqc,0)/at − oancf/at collapses to a plain negative operating-cash-flow ranking for most of the cross-section, so the expression does not compute the "acquisition funding gap" the hypothesis describes and largely reduces to the already-tested cash-flow × liquidity interaction.

The conditioning leg is genuinely changed (short-term debt burden plus current losses rather than current-liability ratio and cash), which is a defensible refinement of the inventory-illiquidity theme, though dlc overlaps lct and the proposal does not diagnose why the earlier version had a strong alpha but a null Fama-MacBeth slope.

Conditioning labor-intensity growth on multi-year loss persistence rather than contemporaneous liquidity is a coherent and reasonably novel construction with signs that match the hypothesis, but the heavy mass at zero loss-years plus limited emp coverage risks a thin, lumpy signal.

The investment leg is identical to the already-failed "Resilient Capex Retrenchment" and the conditioning leg substitutes DELTA(che/at) and −DELTA(lct/act) for DELTA(wcap/at), which is largely the same balance-sheet information, making this a cosmetic variant of a signal with an alpha t-stat near zero.

With gdwl zero for many firms, (gdwl − ceq)/at is dominated by −ceq/at and therefore functions mainly as a book-leverage proxy, so the signal is effectively leverage × negative operating cash flow — both a well-known distress composite and close to the already-tested "Goodwill Impairment Pressure".

This is the archive's "Liquidity-Stressed Acquisition Spend" with the identical distress composite and only a 3-year TS_MAX smoothing applied to the same acquisition-intensity leg, a cosmetic persistence tweak rather than a substantively different mechanism.
Expression is literally the archived "Cash-Flow-Strained Capex Acceleration" with RANK swapped for IND_RANK plus a winsorization, i.e., a pure normalization variant with no new economic content.

It recombines two archived components but replaces the generic liquidity composite with a genuinely different conditioning state — an internal capex-versus-operating-cash funding gap — and the sign logic is internally consistent, though it sits in an already heavily mined asset-renewal family.

The two legs are mechanically entangled — high invt/act shrinks the (act - invt) denominator of the second term — so the product largely amplifies inventory concentration rather than testing a true interaction, and it overlaps directly with the archived "Inventory Liquidity Trap"/"Continuous Inventory Liquidity Squeeze".

Conditioning capex acceleration on short-term debt share of total liabilities is a distinct rollover-risk channel not yet tested (archive used lct/act, oancf, or dlc/at with inventory), and the expected negative sign follows naturally from the expression.

This differs from the archived "Non-Goodwill Intangible Loss Build" only by adding IND_RANK and swapping one highly correlated unprofitability proxy set (oancf/re) for another (ni/liquidity), which is a cosmetic variant of an already weak signal.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "Distressed Asset Renewal Surge" (identical renewal leg, with lct/act simply swapped for dlc/lt inside the same SUMRANK distress conditioner already used in "Soft-Asset Rollover Fragility"), so it tests no new economic channel and is dominated by the archive's stronger "Renewal Funding Shortfall."

Both legs are increasing in capex (acceleration of capx/ppent and the capx-minus-oancf gap), so the product is largely a monotone repackaging of high capital spending rather than a genuine conditional interaction, and it recombines legs already tested in "Cash-Flow-Strained Capex Acceleration" and "Renewal Funding Shortfall."

The signal is essentially the well-known asset-growth anomaly (PP&E plus inventory expansion) crossed with the same distress conditioner already used in at least four archived signals, and its two component channels were separately tested in "Demand-Mismatched Capacity Build" and "Liquidity-Strained Inventory Build."

This is a mechanical leg swap—the exact stale-inventory leg from "Stale Inventory Leverage Overhang" paired with the exact SUMRANK(dlc/lt, NEG oancf/at) conditioner from "Soft-Asset Rollover Fragility"—with no new mechanism and a high likelihood of simply reproducing the earlier alpha.

Leg one is verbatim from "Soft-Asset Rollover Fragility" and leg two verbatim from "Renewal Funding Shortfall," and because intangible-intensive firms typically have low capex the funding-gap conditioner is likely to be a weak, largely orthogonal (or even attenuating) modifier rather than a substantive refinement.

This is a legitimate functional-form repair of the unstable sstk/(capx+aqc) denominator in "Dilutive Noninvestment Rescue" with a coherent hypothesis and matching sign, though it reuses the identical distress conditioner and sits close to the known share-issuance/external-finance anomaly, limiting its novelty.

The second leg negates DELTA(ppent/ppegt), directly contradicting the archive's "Distressed Asset Renewal Surge" (where *rising* net/gross PPE with the identical distress conditioner gave fmb −2.78 and alpha −0.052) and echoing the wrong-signed "Deferred Maintenance Distress" result, and it is also internally awkward because gross-PPE growth mechanically raises net/gross PPE, so the two SUMRANK legs partly offset.

A defensible reorientation of the heavily mined inventory leg from static liquidity composition to contemporaneous financing flows (rising current liabilities plus low cash), though it remains an incremental cousin of "Liquidity-Strained Inventory Build" / "Inventory Liquidity Trap" and rests on the well-known inventory-growth anomaly for its base leg.

This is the most genuinely novel proposal in the set — it deliberately inverts the usual "cash build is good" prior by conditioning tangible-asset runoff on simultaneous cash accumulation and pretax losses, giving a liquidation/fire-sale interpretation not tested by the leverage-conditioned "Levered Tangible Asset Runoff," and the expression matches the stated hypothesis cleanly.

This is a near-mechanical recombination of already-tested legs — aqc/at with a liquidity/profitability conditioner ("Liquidity-Stressed Acquisition Spend") and DELTA(gdwl/at) with a distress conditioner ("Goodwill Build Equity Erosion") — and since goodwill growth is largely a consequence of acquisition spending the two SUMRANK legs are highly collinear, making it a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

Substituting short-term debt issuance for equity issuance in the previously tested "Rescue Issuance Investment Gap" changes the economic channel from dilution to rollover/liquidity plugging and is dimensionally coherent, but the base leg overlaps the published net-debt-issuance anomaly and the distress conditioner is the archive's most reused pair, capping upside.

It opens a receivables/other-current-asset channel untouched by the archive's inventory-dominated working-capital work and the expression matches the hypothesis, but the base leg is close to the published working-capital accruals anomaly, so the incremental content rests entirely on the liquidity-and-weak-sales conditioning.

The DELTA(ppent/ppegt) renewal leg has already been tested against three separate distress conditioners in the archive (Distressed Asset Renewal Surge, Renewal Funding Shortfall, Renewal Payoff Failure), so swapping in a fourth cash-and-maturity conditioner is a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively new mechanism.

This is Maturity-Wall Capex Acceleration with the dlc/lt level replaced by its one-year change — a minimal level-to-change tweak that also compounds a noisy second difference (ACCEL) with a noisy first difference, making it more likely to weaken than clarify the archived result.

Directly rediscovers Liquidity-Stressed Acquisition Spend with only one of two conditioner components swapped (lct/act to NEG(ceq/at), NEG(oancf/at) retained), in a channel already mined six ways in the archive, and the underlying acquirer-underperformance-times-distress effect is close to published anomaly territory.

Shifting from labor-growth flows to the industry-relative level of employee intensity is a real change in the base variable rather than a cosmetic tweak and the fixed-cost-plus-rollover-risk logic is internally consistent, but emp/sale is the inverse of the well-studied sales-per-employee productivity signal, so the novelty rests entirely on the conditioning interaction.

This is "Inventory Credit Squeeze Trend" with a single conditioner leg swapped from NEG(che/at) to NEG(re/at); the left leg and the DELTA(dlc/lt) term are unchanged, so it is a cosmetic variant of one of the archive's strongest existing results and will mostly re-estimate the same portfolio.

Direct rediscovery of the archived "Overstaffed Rollover Burden" with the only change being dlc/lt → lct/act in the conditioner — two highly correlated short-term-pressure proxies — leaving the hypothesis and expected mechanism verbatim identical.

The gdwl/sale leg is identical to "Goodwill Revenue-Support Failure" and the goodwill × leverage/weak-profitability interaction is additionally covered by "Goodwill Impairment Pressure," so this is a third permutation of the same conditioner space rather than a new channel.
